title: Symphony no. 5 in C minor, mvt 1 (Allegro con brio)
source_citations: Donald Tovey, Essays in Musical Analysis vol. I (1935)

key_plan.role: Main theme, four-note motive saturation, tonic with motion to V
Horn-call transition modulating to relative major
Lyrical second theme in relative major; closes with PAC
Fragmented motivic working through F minor, G minor, F# diminished; climax on V/V (D major)
Restatement of main theme — with the famous oboe cadenza at m. 268
Second theme transposed to parallel major (picardy-third effect — Schenker emphasizes this)
Long coda back in C minor with motivic intensification — ~25% of movement

notable_cadences.basis: Half cadence followed by the iconic oboe cadenza
Recap second-theme close in parallel major

characteristic_features: Iconic 4-note motive (G-G-G-Eb in C minor; F-F-F-D when transposed) saturates every section
Sonata form with second theme appearing in parallel major in the recap rather than tonic — Schenkerian point of analytical interest
Coda is unusually long for the period (~25% of movement)
common_omr_pitfalls: Dense orchestration: 14+ instrumental parts — OMR voice-splitting often conflates staves
Fast 2/4 tempo with frequent eighth-note arpeggiation — per-measure rhythm fragility expected
Repeat signs in the exposition (mm. 1–124) often confuse OMR — measure numbers may double-count or skip
Hairpin dynamics and sforzando marks are common — DSv2-trained YOLO may miss these (separate from key-plan accuracy)
_notes: Curated 2026-05-24. Measure numbers reflect standard editions (Breitkopf 1809, Eulenburg, Bärenreiter). Differences of ±1 measure between editions are normal — comparison engine should tolerate ±2 around section boundaries.
